- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.25 or below) in the recent history, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent price spikes; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price drop (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive for 3+ days, model tends to over-forecast; apply a 3–7% downward correction to avoid overshoot.
- Model frequently misreads sentiment momentum: if sentiment turns positive after a negative spike, forecast often lags; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment adjustment to forecast curve.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates downward trends after 10+ consecutive days of low sentiment; apply 3–5% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
